rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A landlord may recover possession of a residential unit only by consent or court eviction, and must have good cause to evict or fail to renew a lease. Every good-cause eviction except nonpayment requires a detailed written Notice to Quit (and sometimes a Notice to Cease), and a judgment for possession must be entered before the tenant must move.
rules.key_value: Warrant for possession not issued until 3 business days after judgment; tenant then has 3 business days to move

exempt_if.text: two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units

exempt_if.name: transient_or_seasonal_lodging
exempt_if.text: hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant

exempt_if.name: family_trust_unit
exempt_if.text: unit held in trust on behalf of a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it

coverage.summary: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units, transient or seasonal hotel/motel/guest house occupants, and certain family-trust units are exempt.

rules.quoted_span: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). There are several grounds for a good cause eviction. Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord in a written notice to the tenant.
